extracted.intended_audience: artists, craftsmen, architects, art historians and students of ornament/architecture
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for producing and judging grotesque ornament and related architectural/ornamental art — distinguishing noble from ignoble grotesque, relations to picturesque and beauty, and moral/psychological sources of grotesque effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose feasible artistic aim (satire/character vs beauty)
rubrics_metrics.description: The workingman who turns his attention partially to art will probably, and wisely, choose to do that which he can do best, and indulge the pride of an effective satire rather than subject himself to assured mortification in the pursuit of beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the artist lacks the finer instincts or leisure to achieve 'perfection of lines and harmonies of color', he should pursue forms (character, satire, quaint fancy) at which he can succeed. Attempting solemn beauty without the requisite power leads to comparative failure. This is not a moral failing but a practical choice suited to recreational or subordinate work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque as 'art of the wayside' — delight in producer's enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: Grotesque is generally the art of the wayside, produced in recreation by minds more or less blunted or encumbered; its delightfulness ought mainly to consist in those very imperfections which mark it for work done in times of rest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the imperfect, playful, and recreative origin of grotesque pieces: the spectator's pleasure comes from sympathy with the maker's enjoyment rather than from strict critical accuracy. Assess grotesque work by the tone, knowledge, wit, love of truth, and kindness of its producers, and by the strength of feeling they give forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish grotesque from picturesque (no conflation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Picturesque is 'parasitical sublimity' — sublimity belonging to external or accidental characters of a thing, not to the thing itself; grotesque elements are produced by the fancy of man and are distinct from picturesque ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'picturesque' to cover grotesque inventions. Picturesque elements (weathering, knots, irregular shingles) often add pleasure to grotesque work but are accidental/parasital; grotesque is generative from human fancy. When judging, separate accidental, time-wrought charm (picturesque) from imaginative, hand-made grotesqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine picturesque elements to strengthen grotesque
rubrics_metrics.description: The picturesque element, usually given by ruggedness or time, adds very largely to the pleasurableness of grotesque work, especially to inferior kinds; yet it is not to be confounded with grotesqueness itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grotesque lacks grandeur, unite it with picturesque qualities (light/shadow, fractures, weather-stains) to increase its appeal. Use natural, accidental textures to lend weight to fanciful inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inordinate playfulness that produces incoherence and monstrosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Art produced by minds indulging in unnecessary play tends to be refined and sensual but feeble; in the continual pursuit of pleasure it becomes restless and dissatisfied, seeking excitement in exaggerations, incoherencies, and monstrosities — an incongruous chain of hackneyed graces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware excessive, idly-thrown ornamentation and manufactured prettinesses or sublimities. If pursuit of amusement or excitement drives the design, the result will be frivolous, incoherent, or impotently malicious rather than powerful or true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity: grotesque must arise from true feeling, not manufactured terror
rubrics_metrics.description: True grotesque arises from real feeling (involuntary apathy, mockery, or deep imaginative temper) and is therefore real and forcible; false grotesque is a manufactured terribleness sought out and elaborated by a frivolous or apathetic mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the terror/awfulness in work is taken from life and experience (authentic) or contrived as an effect (manufactured). Authentic grotesque will appal because the maker himself was appalled; manufactured grotesque lacks force and reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground monstrous forms in observation of nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The master of the true grotesque, though possibly ignorant in craft, never saw a serpent, bird, or lizard without learning of their inner nature; his creatures, however monstrous, will have profound relations with the true — they will 'bite and fly'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even fanciful or monstrous figures must be informed by acute observation so they behave with believable life. Lack of natural insight makes extravagances ineffective: grossness without terror or vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not squander high skill on base or frivolous ornament (avoid 'base grotesque')
rubrics_metrics.description: When great care, skill, and science are applied to trivial or idle grotesque, the result is base — skilful minds degraded to produce nonsense; if we can draw the human form perfectly, we have no business to cut it off and make a toy of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the seriousness of subject to the level of skill employed. Highly competent artists should not apply their powers to mere elaborations of nonsense; such misuse implies deficiency in earnestness or thoughtfulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornamentation should become rational as knowledge increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactly in proportion as the ignorance and rudeness of the workman diminish, must ornamentation become rational, and the grotesqueness disappear; the noblest lessons may be taught in ornamentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage meaningful, informed ornament that can convey solemn truths (e.g., biblical narrative in borders). As makers gain knowledge, aim for reasoned design rather than retaining grotesque merely from habit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mockery and satire in grotesque to instruct about vice
rubrics_metrics.description: Folly and sin may be represented under the most ridiculous forms; such satire was formerly thrown into noble art to make mankind feel that wickedness is as contemptible as it is hateful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical grotesque is appropriate where moral instruction is intended: depict vices as ridiculous to inculcate contempt for wickedness. This use is acceptable and historically grounded in cathedral sculpture and folk ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess grotesque by the maker's moral/psychological tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Grotesque is noble or inferior first according to the tone of the minds which have produced it (knowledge, wit, love of truth, kindness), and secondly by the degree of strength they have given forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating grotesque, attend to the ethical and emotional tenor behind the work. A work of good heart and intelligence may be delightful despite imperfections; malevolent or stupid intent marks ignoble grotesque.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grotesque subjects often unite terror elements of Death and Sin
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper subjects of human fear are twofold: those which have the power of Death, and those which have the nature of Sin; grotesque subjects will often unite expression of vice and danger, regarded in a particular temper (apathy, mockery, diseased imaginativeness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grotesque aims at the terrible, ensure it draws on these deep subjects and the appropriate temper. Distinguish playful engagements with terror (which may be noble) from shallow or mocking treatment that fails to apprehend the underlying seriousness.
